heroTitle: Installable expert flows for every AI coding tool you use.
heroBody: FlaiOS Agents is the agent shelf for your AI Flow OS: code review, product design, growth, data, operations, and safety specialists packaged for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, VSCode, Trae, and portable AGENTS.md workflows.
heroSubline: Stop rewriting prompts and moving habits by hand. Pick one agent or a flow pack, then let every AI call run through a clearer, controlled workflow.
packsTitle: Install a coordinated AI workflow, not a lonely prompt.

usage.title: FlaiOS Agents is not another chat box. It is the control layer for the tools you already use.
usage.body: The website helps you browse, filter, and copy install commands. The actual work happens in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, VSCode Copilot, Trae, and similar tools. Each agent is a readable, auditable, portable workflow file.

steps.title: Choose
steps.body: Pick a focused specialist, or install a flow pack such as solo-founder-pack or code-quality-pack.

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Copy the generated command and write the agent files into your project or target tool config directory.

steps.title: Run
steps.body: Return to the target AI tool and describe the task naturally; the generated agent, rule, or skill constrains the workflow, outputs, and safety boundary.

usage.noteBody: FlaiOS Agents is the agent layer of your AI Flow OS: the website is for choosing, the CLI is for installing, and your AI tools are where the flows run.

codex.where: Install as Codex skills, then call the specialist by task intent inside Codex.
notes: Best for repo work, code review, debugging, research workflows, and repeatable local tasks.
Use collections when you want a ready-made working team instead of one specialist.

claude.where: Install as Claude Code subagent markdown files under .claude/agents.
notes: Best for subagent-style delegation inside a project.
Generated files are portable markdown, so you can inspect and edit them.

cursor.where: Install as Cursor rule files under .cursor/rules.
notes: Best for project-level behavior presets and repeatable coding rules.
Use focused agents for review, frontend, backend, product, and naming tasks.

opencode.where: Install as OpenCode agent markdown under .opencode/agents.
notes: Best for terminal-native workflows and repository assistants.
Use --target all if you want to prepare every platform at once.
Best for project instructions that travel with the repo.
Keep sensitive or personal workflow rules out of public repos.

trae.where: Install as Trae-compatible prompt markdown under .trae/agents.
notes: Best for product, growth, Chinese-market, and coding assistant workflows.
The generated prompt remains readable and editable.
